title: 99 Bends to Heaven's Gate, or 24 WWII Switchbacks — Which Drive? | China Travel Expert
description:
Two of China's most jaw-dropping mountain roads. If you could only drive one, which would it be?

First, Tongtian Avenue — the "99-Bend Road" that climbs Tianmen Mountain in Zhangjiajie, Hunan: 10.8 km of tarmac with 99 hairpin bends, rising from about 200 m to 1,300 m at the foot of Heaven's Gate. Visitors ride official scenic shuttle buses up it; private cars aren't allowed.

Second, the 24-Zig Road near Qinglong in Guizhou: just 4 km long but folded into 24 switchbacks up a steep slope. Finished in 1935, it became a vital stretch of the wartime supply route — convoys of fully loaded trucks hauled thousands of tons of supplies up it each month in the 1940s before it was "lost" to history and rediscovered in 1995.

🧭 Expert Tip: for the 99 bends you don't self-drive — take the scenic shuttle and sit on the valley side for the view down the hairpins; for the 24-Zig, the classic photo is from the viewing platform above, not the road itself.
